title: yunta event
description: One event of a run's log: the envelope and the payload of its `kind`, side by side in one object

AccountLimit.description:
The account's limit, as the session or the forge reported it: where it
came from, when it resets if it said so, and the words it came with.

resets_at.description: Absolute: the moment the limit lifts, when the source named one.

AdapterId.description: An adapter id: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

AgentMessagePayload.description:
What a session reported while it ran, and never the words it said: a
tool it called, the usage it reported, or the digest of a note.

cached_input_tokens.description:
The part of `input_tokens` the CLI read from its cache, when it
says: a part of the input, never added to it.

note.description: A note's size and digest: what the log keeps of a note's words.

target.description:
What the tool acted on. Absent for a message that is not a tool
call, and for a log written before the engine recorded it.

text.description:
The words an older log stored as a note's text. A note written now
carries its digest instead.

AgentMessageType.description:
Which report of a session an `agent_message` is: a tool it called, the
usage it reported, or a note it wrote.

AgentName.description: An agent name: printable ASCII without whitespace

AgentSessionOpenedPayload.description:
A session opened on an adapter's CLI: the first fact of every session,
with the id it is resumed by, what it runs with and what it may reach.

agent.description:
The agent the session worked as, when the node or its runner named
one.

capabilities.description:
What the adapter declared it can do, as it stood when the session
opened.

confinement.description: The confinement the session was opened under.

continues.description:
The session this one resumes: the same conversation, picked up
after the answer to what it asked. Absent for a session that
opened fresh.

effort.description:
The effort the session was asked to reason with; absent when the
node and its runner left it to the CLI.

fence.description:
How much of this session the adapter's fence covered — derived
from what it built, never declared. Absent when it built none.
The level travels once, in `capabilities.fence`.

model.description:
The model the CLI reported for the session; absent when it
reported none.

session_id.description:
The CLI's own id for the session: what a resume hands back to the
adapter to pick the same conversation up.

task_id.description:
The task a loop's session works. Absent for a node's own session,
and on a log written before sessions named their task.

Approval.description: Where a person approved a gate.

oneOf.description: At the console, on the menu the run asked with.
On the forge, by a review.
On the forge, by merging the change.

ArtifactAcceptedPayload.description:
One artifact the run holds: what it is, the bytes it is made of, and
how the run came by it.

This is what makes an artifact a fact of the log rather than a file
somebody may have replaced: the identity says which artifact, the
hash says which content, and the envelope's `node_id` says who
produced it — absent for what a run acquires without a node of its
own (a `document` input, a mount, a promotion).

The field is named `artifact`, not `kind`, for the reason
[`ArtifactWrittenPayload::artifact_kind`] gives: the event
envelope's own internally-tagged discriminant already claims `kind`
in the serialized JSON, and a colliding field name silently corrupts
the payload.

artifact.description: What the artifact is: what a reader asks for it by.

content_hash.description:
The hash of the accepted bytes, the object under `objects/` that
holds them.

origin.description: How the run came by it.

ArtifactFailure.description:
Why one declared artifact did not close.

The variants answer the one question that decides what is worth
doing next: rewriting the content reaches [`Content`](Self::Content),
nothing this node writes reaches [`File`](Self::File) or
[`Undelivered`](Self::Undelivered), and nothing this run does at all
reaches [`Unheld`](Self::Unheld), because the artifact is another
run's to produce.

oneOf.description: The file itself. No rewrite of its content reaches this.

Declared by a node the run's own log answers for, and never
handed over: the node ended without the document it owes.

No path, for the same reason [`Unheld`](Self::Unheld) has none.
Such a document never is a file on its way in — a session hands
it over through its submission tool, the engine derives it from
what the node posted — so the close opened nothing and there is
no file to name.

artifact.description:
What the node owes: the identity, which is what a log
answers by.

node.description: The node that declared it and ended owing it.

oneOf.description: The file is there and its content is not what its kind declares.

Declared here and held by no run that could hand it over: the
run that owes it — a `kind: workflow` node's child, or the run a
mount names as its source — answers with nothing under this
identity.

A node of composition writes no file, so there is nothing on
disk to be missing and nothing this run does reaches the
artifact: producing it is another run's to do.

artifact.description:
What the run was asked for: the identity, which is what a
log answers by.

producer.description:
The node of that run the artifact was asked of, when the
reference names one. `None` when the question is about the
run as a whole, which is what a `kind: workflow` node asks
of its child.

run.description:
The run that was asked and holds none of it — where a reader
goes to look.

ArtifactId.description:
What an artifact is, which is what a reader asks for it by.

An artifact the engine interprets is identified by its kind: a run
holds one tasks document, whoever produced it, so a reader asks for
the kind and never needs to know the file name its workflow chose.
One the engine only carries is identified by the name the workflow
declared, which is the only thing that distinguishes it from any
other opaque artifact.

ArtifactKind.description:
A document the engine reads and validates, as opposed to an artifact
it only checks for existence. The kind fixes the document's shape, so
it is what every door — the workflow's own `kind:`, `yunta schema`,
the `document_shape` tool, a failed read's report — names it by.

The bar for another kind is high: a document whose data the engine
needs, to decide or to count — never one it only carries. A file it
only carries is opaque: the engine knows that it exists and what it
hashes to, and its structure is its writer's, which is why the
knowledge a run distills stays prose for a person and an agent to read.

ArtifactOrigin.description:
Where an artifact came from, as the log spells it: the recorded
origins and `legacy` are one tagged set on the wire, while in Rust a
fresh acceptance can only name a [`RecordedOrigin`]. `serde` moves
between the two here, so the type the engine holds is not shaped by
the file it is written to.

ArtifactRefId.description:
What a reference names an artifact by: `kind:` for a document the
engine reads, `name:` for a file it only carries.

The mapping form of [`ArtifactSpec`], for the references that carry
more than the artifact itself — a `context:` source and a `mounts:`
entry also name the node it comes from, and a mount also names what
the child carries it as.

ArtifactSubmittedPayload.description:
What a session offered as a whole document, and what the engine
answered. Every hand-over is kept, accepted or refused; one accepted is
also an `artifact_accepted` of origin `submitted`, the artifact the run
holds.

artifact_kind.description:
Named `artifact_kind`, not `kind`, for the reason
[`ArtifactWrittenPayload`] gives: the envelope's own tag already
claims `kind` in the serialized JSON.

name.description:
The name of the document's view, `<kind>.yaml`: the node declares
the kind, so a hand-over names nothing of its own.

outcome.description:
Accepted, with the hash of the canonical document the run stores; or
refused, with the whole report, so what was refused and why reads
off the log.

probes.description:
What the engine ran to prove the document, task by task: how each
criterion answered on the tree it ran on, which a later invocation
takes for that tree. Empty for a document whose commands nothing
runs, and on a log written before the field.

artifact_kind.description:
The artifact's declared `kind:` when it has one — what
lets `derive()` recognize a `questions` artifact without reading
any file (state comes from events alone). `None` for opaque
artifacts and for logs written before the field existed (tolerant
reader). Named `artifact_kind`, not `kind`: the event
envelope's own internally-tagged discriminant already claims
`kind` in the serialized JSON, and a colliding field name
silently corrupts the payload.

AskedScope.description:
What a session asked for: the paths, and its own reason, absent when a
red criterion located the refused writes.

AskingOpenedPayload.description:
A person at the engine's terminal is being asked something: a gate's
choice, an escalation, a round of questions. The answer lands as the
event that resolves what was asked; this one says when the asking
began, which only the engine that put the question knows. Audit: no
ledger moves.

task_id.description:
The task whose work is waiting on the answer, when a task's
session asked; absent when the node asked for itself.

AuthorGate.description: Who an author's gate addresses, as its workflow names them.

BaselineCapturedPayload.description:
What the suite a run's lineage declared did on the tree the run
opens on, and whose measurement it is.

duration_ms.description: How long the measurement took. Absent where `tree` is.

hash.description:
The sha256 of what the suite printed to stdout, which the
measuring run keeps under its `baseline/`.

origin.description:
Whose measurement this is. A log written before the field reads
[`BaselineOrigin::Measured`], which is what such a log meant.

tree.description:
The git tree the suite was measured on: what a later invocation
takes the measurement's answer for. Absent for a measurement the
run was born holding — it speaks for the tree its measuring run
opened on — and on a log written before the field.

BaselineHeldPayload.description:
What one project command `baseline.held` names did on the tree the
run's lineage measured its suite on, and whose measurement it is. Green,
it holds every task of the run as the suite does; red, it holds none.

command.description: What the project runs for it.

duration_ms.description: How long it took. Absent where `tree` is.

name.description: The command's name, as `commands:` declares it.

tree.description:
The git tree it was measured on; absent for a measurement the run
was born holding.

BaselineOrigin.description:
Who took the measurement a run holds: this run, or the root of the
lineage it was born into.

A lineage measures once. A run born of another — a `kind: workflow`
child, a promotion successor — is born holding the root's
measurement, so every comparison anywhere in the lineage answers the
same question: what worked before the invocation started.

oneOf.description: This run ran the suite itself, on its first wake.

The run was born holding it; `run` is the root that measured,
never the parent it was handed down through.

BaselineResults.description:
What the suite reported: the code it exited with, and the tail a
reader sees without opening what the measuring run kept.

BestEffortFailedPayload.description:
A best-effort step that failed and that the run carried on past: the
step, and the cause its source gave.

BestEffortStep.description: The closed set of best-effort steps the log names.

oneOf.description: Closing the MCP client after its one query.

BudgetCap.description:
`limits.max_tokens_per_run`, and the input and output tokens the log
says the run spent against it.

Capabilities.description:
An adapter's declared capabilities. Constant for the
lifetime of the adapter — the engine consults this before asking
for anything, and never emulates what is not declared.

Lives in `yunta-core` rather than `yunta-adapters` because it is also
the shape of `agent_session_opened`'s `capabilities` field;
both the event log and the `Adapter` trait
share this one definition instead of duplicating it.

custom_agents.description:
Can add an agent's instructions (`SessionRequest.agent`), which the
run resolved from its own definition, to its CLI's own.

fence.description:
What this adapter can build to keep a session's writes inside
its fence. `None` means nothing: the post-check diff is the only
thing that catches a write outside the scope. A log written
before the fence existed carries `edit_hooks` instead, which this
field's `default` reads as `None`.

mid_session_token_cap.description:
Whether the CLI reports a session's token use while the session
runs, so the run's token cap can end the session as it passes the
cap. Absent, the cap is checked when the session ends.

network_isolation.description:
Can confine a session's process to no network access, enforcing a
node's `network: false`. Declarative policy is never an OS sandbox
Yunta core promises: where this is absent, a node's
`network: false` degrades with `capability_degraded` — recorded for
policy and audit, never enforced.

resume_session.description: Can resume a previous conversation via `resume()`.

run_tools.description: Can connect to Yunta's per-run MCP server as a client.

skills.description:
Can mount skill directories (`SessionRequest.skills`) by the
CLI's native mechanism. A skill is added instruction,
never correctness: absence degrades with `capability_degraded`,
never a fatal error.

stop_refusals.description:
Whether the CLI keeps a session going after the engine refuses two stops in a row over
different states of the work.

tool_naming.description:
How the model in this adapter's sessions calls a tool of a server
the adapter mounts — the name every text the engine shows a
session gives a run tool, so a session never calls a name its CLI
does not have.

usage_reporting.description: Emits trustworthy token usage in the stream.

Capability.description:
One capability an adapter can declare: the closed set of
[`Capabilities`] fields, spelled the way `capability_degraded` records
them (`resume_session`, `run_tools`, …). The engine names the
capability it consulted with this type, so a degradation can never
cite a capability no adapter has.

CapabilityDegradedPayload.description:
A capability the engine consulted and an adapter does not declare, and
what the engine did in its place: a fallback the log states, never a
silent one.

adapter.description: The adapter that does not declare it.

capability.description: The capability the engine consulted and the adapter does not declare.

policy.description:
What the engine did instead. A log that stored a sentence under
`policy_applied` reads it back as `PolicyApplied::Recorded`.

CapabilityUse.description: What a node needs a capability for.

oneOf.description: The node is in a blackboard group, which the run tools carry.
The node declares a typed artifact of `kind`, which the run tools carry.
The node is a loop, whose task sessions read their task through the run tools.

Channel.description: How a round of questions was answered.

oneOf.description:
Nobody answered: every question was optional, and the engine closed
the round on what each one assumes.

ChildRefusal.description: Why a composed workflow the run could not start.

oneOf.description: No workflow answers to the name; `problem` is the catalog's own account.
Its file does not read as a workflow.
Its own check refuses it; `rules` are the codes of what it refused.

The inputs the node hands it do not fit what it declares; `problem`
says what does not fit.

ChildRunCreatedPayload.description: The parent's `kind: workflow` node is the envelope's own `node_id`.

child_run_id.description:
The child run: a run of its own, with its own log, and the reference
to it that never changes.

ChildRunFinishedPayload.description: A child run reached its terminal state, and what it spent.

tokens.description:
The child run's whole derived spend at its close — a child
run's usage always aggregates up into its parent, so replay adds
it to the parent's own total. That means a promotion *chain*'s
every member counts exactly once, resumes included, and the
parent node's own `node_finished` carries no child tokens
(they'd double-count). Additive: events logged before this field
existed parse as zero.

Claim.description:
What an escalation says happened: a claim the engine states about a node
or the run, or a summary whoever escalated wrote.

On the log an engine claim is an object tagged by `claim`, and a plain
string reads back as a summary the escalating party wrote.

Cleaned.description:
What `on_finish.cleanup` could not take away: the run's worktree, or the
branch it ran on.

CommandExit.description:
What a command that exited non-zero left behind: whose command it was
when it was not the node's own `run:`, the code it exited with, the
last lines it printed — stdout, then stderr, as a reader reads them —
and the run object holding everything it printed.

The tail is what a person deciding about the failure reads first, so
it rides on the event; the whole output stays in the run's object
store, where a reader who needs more than the tail finds it by hash.

CommandName.description: A command name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

CommandOrigin.description: Who ran a command that is not the node's own `run:`.

oneOf.description: An external executor the node delegated its work to.
One of the node's hooks, as the workflow wrote its command.

Commands.description: What the commands may do; the worktree is what tools may write (judged by the fence's globs).

CommitSha.description: A commit sha: 7 to 64 lowercase hex digits: a git object id, abbreviated or full

ConfigKey.description: A config key a node cannot run without.

oneOf.description:
`baseline_compare` compares against what the lineage measured
before its first node, and `baseline.suite` is what it measures.

`coverage_gate` runs `coverage.cmd` and holds it to
`coverage.threshold`.
`kind: executor` runs the binary registered under its name.
A session opens on a runner: the node's own, or `defaults.runner`.

`run: { command: <name> }` runs what the project declares under
`commands:` for that name.

`kind: pull_request` opens its pull request through the forge
under `forge:`.

`kind: pull_request` pushes the run's own branch, which only a run
with a worktree of its own has.

ConfinementRecord.description: What the session was allowed to reach; absent on logs written before it.

worktree.description: What the session's file tools may write under the checkout.

ConsoleGate.description:
An external gate answered at the console: its claim says why no forge
answers, so it carries nothing more.

ContentHash.description: A content hash: 64 lowercase hex digits, the SHA-256 of the content

ContextAssembledPayload.description:
What a session was handed before it opened: each context source the
assembly resolved, by the hash of the bytes the run stored for it, and
one hash per stability segment, so two sessions' prefixes compare by
hash and replay names what a session saw without running anything.

segment_hashes.description:
Keys are `"stable" | "run-stable" | "volatile"` (the fixed
stability classes) — kept as plain strings rather than an enum key
to sidestep serde's map-key-as-enum ceremony for no real benefit.

sources.description: Every context source the assembly resolved.

task_id.description:
`Some` when this assembly built one *task's* brief inside a loop
node — the same task-vs-node convention
`ScopeCheckedPayload.task_id` already follows. `None` for a
node-level assembly (a `prompt` node's own context). Additive:
events logged before this field existed parse with `None`.

ContextSourceRef.description:
One resolved `ContextSource` reference in `context_assembled.sources`.
`kind` stays a plain string — the engine fixes the *set* of
builtin source kinds (`files | command | artifact | run-events |
tasks | knowledge | node-output`, `mcp` among them) but never closes
it into an enum, since a pack can add its own sources without
this type needing to change. `content_hash` is what makes every
resolution's event carry a verifiable hash — the hash of exactly
the bytes the run stored under `objects/<content_hash>` for this
source, so replay can name precisely what a session saw without
re-running anything.

absent.description:
The optional `files:` paths this source did not find: the
session got a marker in each one's place, and the hash above
covers that marker. Empty — and absent from the wire — for every
source that found all it read.

Coverage.description:
How much of a session the fence actually covered, derived from what
the adapter could build — never declared.

CriteriaCheckedPayload.description:
What the engine's own run of a task's criteria answered, before or
after the work: the verdict on a task is this, never a session's word.

results.description:
One result per criterion that ran or was answered by an earlier run
on the same tree.

waiting.description:
The guards the check did not run, by command: a criterion that ran
before them — one of the task's own, or a guard — was red, and the
check cannot close the task whatever a later guard answers. Absent
when every guard ran, and in a log written before guards waited.

Criterion.description:
A tasks document criterion, frozen into `task_registered` — the same shape
the tasks parser produces.

cmd.description: The command, as the task declares it.

conclusion.description:
The line the command concluded with, when it printed one: its last
non-empty stdout line, else its last stderr line. Taken when the
result is recorded, so a replay reads what the live run read.
Absent when nothing was printed, and on a log written before the
field.

duration_ms.description:
Wall-clock milliseconds this execution took — the datum
the learned criterion ordering feeds on. `None` for a `reused: true`
result (nothing ran) and for events logged before this field
existed (additive, tolerant reader).

exit_code.description: The code the command exited with.

head.description:
The commit the checkout stood on, kept only for a command that
runs `git`, whose answer can turn on history as well as on files.

output.description:
The run object holding everything the command printed — stdout,
then stderr — with the run's secrets taken out: for a red answer
`reused`, what the run that gave it printed. Absent when the
command printed nothing, for a green answer `reused`, and on a log
written before a run kept what its commands printed.

reused.description:
Whether the answer is one an earlier run of the same command gave on
the same tree, taken without running the command again.

tail.description:
The last lines a criterion that did not pass printed: what a
reader of the log, a person deciding and the next session read to
know why, without opening the object. Empty for one that passed.

tree.description:
The git tree of what the checkout held when the command answered:
what the answer is kept for, so a later invocation can take it for
the same tree. Absent for a check the engine states rather than
runs, and on a log written before the field.

CriterionType.description:
A criterion's kind: a `guard` is green before the work, and the task has
to keep it green.

CriterionUnpassablePayload.description:
A criterion of a task that its session declared no work of the plan
can pass. The engine ran it on the tree the session left and saw it
red; the exit code it saw and the session's reason are recorded. Only
a session's first declaration is. The task does not close on it, and a
loop left with nothing to run fails with `PlanUnpassable`, the failure
a re-route hands to whatever writes the plan again.

criterion.description: The criterion's command, as the plan writes it.

exit_code.description:
The code it exited with on that tree: never zero, and never 126 or
127, which name the environment rather than the work.

Decider.description:
`decided_by`: `rule | person | evidence`, with who the person was, or
which criterion's output was the evidence.

oneOf.description:
What a red criterion of the task printed located the paths: a fact
the engine verified, not a choice anyone made.

Denial.description:
Why a request was denied, typed. The event log keeps this value; the
words a reader sees are written from it where that reader is.

oneOf.description: A person chose an option other than a grant.
A refusal read from its text, from logs written before reasons were typed.

DeniedBy.description: The list of `permissions.commands` that refused a command.

oneOf.description: `permissions.commands.deny` holds a pattern the command matches.
`permissions.commands.allow` is a strict allowlist, and no pattern matches.

DeniedCommand.description:
What the project's permissions refused: the command, and the pattern of
the list that refused it.

DeniedRule.description: What a denial records: the command, or the sentence an older log stored.

anyOf.description: The sentence an older log stored, kept as written.

DepartsFrom.description:
What of the plan a task session departs from: one of the plan's
shapes or decisions by name, one of its own changes by where it is,
one of its criteria by its command, or what it said a person would
see once it was done.

DepartureMenu.description:
The departure from the plan a task's session declared, as its question
is written: the declarations it asks about, the plan's criteria that
accepting stops holding the task to, the node that writes the task's
tests again, and whether accepting is offered at all. Every word of the
question is written from these fields when it is shown.

accept_offered.description:
Whether accepting is offered. False when a test a departure departs
from came with the run and no node of the run writes it again.

deviations.description: What the session declared, as `deviation_declared` records it.

rewritten_by.description: The node that writes the task's tests again, when accepting does.

waived.description:
The commands of the plan's criteria accepting stops holding the
task to. Absent when accepting waives none.

DeviationDeclaredPayload.description:
A task session declared that its work departs from the plan: what
the plan said, what the session did or needs instead, and why. The
task does not close on it until a person answers. The session's words
are kept whole: unlike what it says while it works, a departure is
something it states to the run on purpose.

instead.description: What the work does or needs instead.

planned.description: What the plan says, in the session's words.

DeviationResolvedPayload.description:
A person's answer to what a task's session departed from the plan
on: accepted as it stands, or sent back with what they said.

accepted.description:
Accepted, the task closes as it stands once its criteria pass, less
the plan's criteria it departed from; sent back, its session picks
the work up again with what the person said.

respecified_by.description:
The node that writes the task's tests again, when the person
accepted departing from a test the run's spec gave it.

said.description: What the person said, when they said anything.

Diagnostic.description: One thing that is wrong with a document.

at.description:
Where in the document's text the problem is, when whoever read
the document read it from text: where the parser stopped, or
where the entry the subject names is written. A document handed
over as a structured value has no text, and no place in it.

oneOf.description: The document as a whole, as opposed to an entry inside it.

A criterion names the task it belongs to, so a reader always has
somewhere to look — including when that task's own id is what
could not be read.
One task's spec, named by the task it holds.

A node of a workflow, for a rule about the graph the file
declares.

The document does not parse into its kind: an unknown key, a
value of the wrong type, an id that is not one. `path` locates
the offending value from the document's root (`tasks[1].scope`),
and is empty when the root itself is the problem; `message` is
what the deserializer said about that value, which names the key
and what it expected.

A rule the document broke once it was readable — the tasks document's own
registration rules and their siblings. `code` is what a receipt
counts; `words` says what the rule found.

DiscardedCandidate.description:
A candidate the resolution passed over before the one it chose, and
why. A candidate after the chosen one was never tried, and is not one.

DistillStep.description: The step of `on_finish.distill` that git refused.

DocumentKind.description:
What kind of document a report is about.

Every document this system reads is held to a shape and to rules,
and reports what it found the same way — so a workflow that breaks
its own rules reaches a reader in the shape a tasks document already
does. The two are separate arms because they are read at different
moments by different doors: a workflow before any run, an artifact
at a node's close.

anyOf.description: The workflow file a run is created from.
A document a node produces and the engine reads.

DocumentRef.description:
Which document a report is about: the kind that fixes its shape, and
where a reader opens it.

A document always has a kind. An artifact the engine never
interprets has no shape to demand and therefore no content to report
on; what can go wrong with one is a [`FileProblem`] instead. An
artifact another run owes has no document at all, and names none.

path.description: As a reader would type it to open the file.

Effort.description:
How long the model reasons before it answers. The four levels every
adapter's CLI accepts, each handed to it under the CLI's own name for
them; a level one CLI has and another lacks is no level here.

EngineError.description:
What a failed engine step records: the step, and what its failing call
reported of itself, or the sentence an older log stored.

anyOf.description: The engine step that failed on its own, with what names it.

report.description: What the failing call reported, absent when the step has no error to report.

oneOf.description: The stdin an executor reads could not be serialized.
The node's context could not be resolved.
A session found its staged record already taken.
A child run's state roots could not be frozen.
A child workflow's manifest could not be frozen.
A child run's worktree could not be prepared.

EventPayload.description: All event kinds, internally tagged by `kind`; published in `events.json`.

Evidence.description:
The facts a record holds beside the claim it rests on, as the log keeps
them.

The pair is the point: the claim says what happened and these facts are
the *record* it rests on, so neither one repeats the other. A producer
that writes the cause into both leaves every surface printing it twice,
under a heading that promised something new.

Untagged, with `Prose` last: a payload carrying a list reads as
[`Evidence::Facts`], and a log written before evidence was data
carries one string and reads back as [`Evidence::Prose`], which
reads as the single unlabelled fact it always was. That tolerance
is the rule for what is persisted and versioned, and it is why no
reader needs to know which version wrote the line it is looking at.

anyOf.description:
What this binary writes: the labelled facts, in the order a
reader meets them.

One string, as an older log recorded it. Only reading produces
this; nothing in this workspace writes one.

ExecutionEnvironment.description:
What the engine hands every command it runs — criteria, `bash` nodes,
hooks: the shell that interprets it, and the directories that shell
looks programs up in, in order. A command that works in an agent's

the cap it reached, and the mode a promotion would take the run to,
when the workflow names one.

next_mode.description: The mode a promotion would take the run to, when there is one.

Fact.description:
One fact the engine read off the log: the label a reader scans for,
and the value under it.

The label is optional because not every fact needs one. A cause like
`exit 1` or a sentence like `no forge reachable from this machine`
already names itself, and putting a word in front of it would add
reading without adding meaning; a bare number like `400` says
nothing until `limits.max_tokens_per_run` is in front of it. A fact
that carries a label states it here rather than writing it into the
value, so every surface sets the two apart the same way.

Failure.description:
Why a node failed.

Untagged: each variant is read by the keys it requires, and each requires
at least one key no other variant has. A payload that names none of them
is refused rather than read as some variant. `Message` reads a log line
that carries `outcome:` alone, a failure written as a sentence, so it
comes last. A field the wire always names but may leave `null` is read
with `deserialize_with`, since serde reads a missing `Option` as `None`,
which would let a payload match a variant it does not belong to.

not done until a person answers, and the answer is theirs.

A config key the node cannot run without, left unset in the

A check that judges the run's tree was asked to run again on the

running, since the same command on the same tree answers the same.

Boxed for the same reason as the child refusal: a failure is copied

FenceLevel.description:

Past `limits.max_artifact_bytes`. Both numbers are on the table,

FindingProvedPayload.description:
What a node's work proved of a finding it answered fixed: the

settles the finding; failing is kept, so a person reads that the
evidence did not bear the answer out. The proving node is the

A finding a session offered and the engine did not take, with every

saw.

settled it.

Tasks whose declared criterion no work of the plan can pass: the
