variant has.

The session refused the request: the adapter's message, and the
cause it read from it.

The account's limit, or the forge's, stopped the run. `resets_at` is
absolute: a forge's retry-after is added to the failure's own time.

Tasks of a loop stopped before the loop could finish: each names
the task and why it stopped.
A judging check came out red on the tree it judged.

A composed workflow whose run ended in failure; `child_failure` is
the failure its own log records, when it records one.
A frozen input no longer matches the hash the run was born with.

The engine cannot end a session it asked to stop; its process group may
still run. `session_not_stopped` is what the stop reported; `release_failed`,
what taking back what the session set up reported, when that failed too.

A session or an executor past its wall-clock budget: `after_ms` is the
budget, and `timed` says whose it was.
A task that spends more tokens than its budget.

A template that does not render, and why. `input` is the child's input
the template was rendering, when it was rendering one.

An artifact the run cannot hand over; `problem` says whether its
object is missing or holds other bytes.
A name the engine refuses for an artifact; `problem` says which rule it breaks.

A mount that cannot bring its artifact into the node; `error` says why.
Boxed for the same reason as the child refusal: a failure is copied
through every frame that holds one.

A gate whose person chose `option`, which routes the run to `target`;
`said` is what the person wrote with the choice, when they wrote any.
A person accepted that the tests a task is held to are wrong; `owed_by` owes the fix.

A composed workflow the run could not start. The refusal is boxed: it
is the largest payload a failure carries, and every frame that holds a
failure pays for it.

A composed workflow that would nest past the depth the run allows;
`depth` is the level it would reach, and `workflow` the composed one.
An artifact an external gate hands over that no node of this run produces.

A capability the frozen adapter does not declare, which a node needs;
`used_for` says what for, and `agent` names the agent that asked, when one did.

An engine step failed on its own; `engine_error` names the step, and
what its failing call reported of itself.

A command the project's permissions deny; `denied_rule` is the command and
the list that denies it.
A skill the node names that the run does not hold; `searched` lists the roots it looked in.
A loop that reached the iteration cap the run declares; `loop_cap` is that cap.
A session the engine cannot confine as the run asks; `confinement` says why.
A frozen read that cannot give the node what it asked for; `frozen_read` says why.

A parallel group that failed under its join: for `join: all`, the failed
children with the first first; for `join: any`, every child.

A child that ran with no terminal event when the engine last stopped,
under `on_interrupt: fail_if_uncertain`.
A gate a person rejected from the console, on the approval it asked for.
A plan the planner did not publish, sent back with the flaws it has.
A findings gate with findings at or above its severity.
The loser of a `join: any` race, which a sibling in its group finished ahead of.
A reviewer requested changes on an external gate's pull request, at `reviewed_sha`.

A pull request closed without approval; `closed_pull_request` is its
reference when the forge gave one.

A loop with no task ready and not every task done; `not_ready` names
the tasks that are waiting.
A loop whose run holds no tasks document; `tasks_for` is the loop's node.
A node's runner that did not resolve to an adapter, and why.

Reads a log line that carries `outcome:` alone; no writer creates it.
The words are the sentence an older log stored, kept as written.

NodeFinishedPayload.description:
A node closed on the engine's verdict: what it checked, or what a person
decided. An agent's summary may ride along as the outcome; it never
decides the close.

commit.description:
The commit the node's close made of what it left in the run's own
tree. Absent when it made none: nothing changed, the node landed
its work from a checkout of its own, another node sharing the tree
was still working, or the run works without a tree of its own.

outcome.description: What the node resolved to: a fact the engine checked, or the agent's summary.

tokens_used.description:
What the attempt spent that its close settles. A close a round of
questions deferred carries zero: the round settled what the session
that asked spent.

tree.description:
The run's tree as the node left it, after whatever it landed —
what a check that verified the tree is measured against when
something later changes it. Absent in a log written before it was
recorded, which then says nothing about the tree.

NodeId.description: A node id: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`; a fan-out sibling adds `@` and its runner's name

NodeOutcome.description:
What a node resolved to: a fact the engine checked, or the agent's
own summary of its work.

anyOf.description: The agent's own summary, or a sentence read from a log.

NodeReroutedPayload.description:
`from_node` is the envelope's own `node_id` (the node that failed) —
only the re-route's destination is extra information.

attempt.description:
The retry count against the cap — present only for an
`on_failure` reroute, absent for a gate's routing choice, which
is not a retry and has no cap to count against.

cause.description:
Why control left the node, as data: the failure the node ended
with, or the message a gate's choice states.

max_reroutes.description:
The cap `attempt` counts against, the node's
`on_failure.max_reroutes`; absent where `attempt` is.

origin.description:
Which mechanism rerouted. Old logs, written before the
distinction existed, carry no field and read as `OnFailure`.

NodeStartedPayload.description:
A node's attempt begins: its number, the tree it starts from, and what
it found in the run's tree that nobody had committed.

attempt.description:
The attempt, counted from one. Each time the node runs again — after
a re-route, a restart of an interrupted attempt, a person's choice —
starts the next.

found.description:
The commit made, as this attempt started, of what the run's tree
held that no node had committed — a person's edits while the run
was parked, or what an interrupted attempt left. Absent when there
was nothing to find.

from_tree.description:
The tree this attempt starts from — what its own diff is judged
against when it closes, so a node answers for what it changed and
not for what the run's worktree already held.

Absent in a log written before the audit had a recorded starting
point, and read then as the run's own base: the tolerance every
persisted field here gives a reader older than its writer.

run_scope.description:
For a node scoped to the run (`scope: run`), what the run had
changed since its base when this attempt started — the paths the
attempt may change, fixed here so its close audits against what
it was given. Absent for every other node.

NonEmpty.description:
A `Vec<T>` with at least one element.

Built through [`NonEmpty::new`], which answers `None` for an empty
one, or from a first element and the rest. Reads as a slice. On the
wire it is the plain array, and an empty array does not read.

NonEmpty2.description:
A `Vec<T>` with at least one element.

Built through [`NonEmpty::new`], which answers `None` for an empty
one, or from a first element and the rest. Reads as a slice. On the
wire it is the plain array, and an empty array does not read.

NonEmpty3.description:
A `Vec<T>` with at least one element.

Built through [`NonEmpty::new`], which answers `None` for an empty
one, or from a first element and the rest. Reads as a slice. On the
wire it is the plain array, and an empty array does not read.

NonEmpty4.description:
A `Vec<T>` with at least one element.

Built through [`NonEmpty::new`], which answers `None` for an empty
one, or from a first element and the rest. Reads as a slice. On the
wire it is the plain array, and an empty array does not read.

NoteDigest.description: A note a session wrote, as the log keeps it: its size and the head of its digest.

ObjectProblem.description:
Why the bytes an artifact names cannot be handed over: the run's store
holds no object under the hash, or the object holds other bytes.

oneOf.description: The run holds no object under `hash`.

The object under `hash` holds content that hashes to `found`: these
are not the bytes the run accepted.

OnInterrupt.description:
A node's crash-recovery policy — the full triple of options.

`restart_node` runs the node again from its start, as a new attempt:
the context it is handed is rebuilt from the run's data, so the attempt
can always begin, but its effect has to be safe to repeat.
`fail_if_uncertain` is for an effect that is not — a notification with
no key to dedupe on, a charge: a resume that finds the node running with
no terminal pauses for a person instead of guessing how it ended.

oneOf.description:
Continue the same agent conversation — the
`session_id` the log recorded (`agent_session_opened`) is
handed back to the adapter's `resume`. Only `kind: prompt` opens
a node-scoped session, so `check` refuses the explicit
declaration anywhere else; an adapter without the
`resume_session` capability — or a crash before any session
opened — degrades to `restart_node` with an explicit
`capability_degraded` event, never silently. As a *config default*
(`defaults.on_interrupt`) it applies where a session exists;
kinds without one (bash/check/…, and a loop's per-task sessions)
restart, which is the only meaning the policy can have there.

OptionId.description: An option id: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

OwedScope.description:
One task's request for scope, owed a person's decision: what it asked
to be allowed to write, and why, in its session's own words. `reason` is
absent when a red criterion of the task located the refused writes, rather
than its session.

PauseReason.description:
Why a run is parked, as a fact rather than a sentence.

The log stores this fact. The line a reader sees for a parked run is
composed from it at the border, by the render crate, so every surface
that shows the pause says it the same way.

oneOf.description:
A decision is waiting on a person, with the escalation that asks
it. Serde goes through `GateWaitingPayload`; a read does not
re-check the claim.
A person stopped the run while it was running.

A person stopped a run whose engine was already dead: the
orphaned process groups were killed from outside and the pause
written on the engine's behalf, so the log says who ended the
run and that nothing of it was still alive to ask.
The run reached `limits.max_tokens_per_run`.

The disk has `available` bytes free, and going on would take
`need` more where `keep_free` must stay free.

A loop reached `limits.max_loop_iterations` with tasks still
ready.
A gate is published and the forge has not answered it.

A resume found nodes still running whose fate it cannot tell: each
declares `on_interrupt: fail_if_uncertain`, because its effect is
not safe to repeat, and a person verifies how it ended before
resuming. One such node holds back the whole resume.
A node failed and nothing re-routed it.
The account's limit resets at `at`; the run resumes detached then.

Nothing is runnable: `node` waits on `on`, which this pass left
unresolved.
A gate was resolved to abort, with whatever the person wrote.

A child run paused on its own log; the parent names it and keeps
the child's pause.
A node asked questions and no surface could answer them.

A surface answered and the questions refused the reply, with
every way it failed to answer them.
Prose a log carries as one sentence; shown as written.

PermissionProfile.description:
The profile a session runs under. The log reads it as `read_only`,
`edit` or `full`.

Phase.description:
When a task's criteria ran: before its work, where each criterion but a
guard is meant to be red, or after it, where every one has to pass.

Policy.description:
What the engine does when an adapter does not declare a capability it
asked for. A closed set: the engine has one fallback per capability
it consults, and a degradation naming anything else would be a
fallback nobody implemented.

The words a reader is shown for each one are kept outside core, so
the same fallback reads the same way wherever it is shown.

oneOf.description:
`fence` is `None`: the session edits freely and the diff is
judged afterwards.

`usage_reporting` absent: the run's token cap cannot be counted
against this session.
`skills` absent: the session runs with none mounted.

`run_tools` absent, or its server unreachable: the session holds
none of the run's tools.

`network_isolation` absent: `network: false` is recorded, not
enforced.

`resume_session` absent, or nothing to resume: a fresh session
replaces the interrupted one.

`mid_session_token_cap` absent: the CLI reports no usage while a
session runs, so the run's token cap is checked when the session ends.

Precheck.description: What running a proposed criterion found.

oneOf.description: The criterion fails with this exit: the red output a request may cite.
The criterion is not run, so no exit is known.

Precondition.description: What must change before a retry can end differently: the tree, something outside it, or the named input.

oneOf.description: The run's tree has to change first.
Something outside the run's tree has to change first.
The credential the session was refused for has to be fixed.
The model the session asked for has to be one the account can use.
The service accepts requests again, by account or by throttle.
The service the session talks to has to answer.
The command has to run: it is installed and executable.
A person lifts the loop's iteration cap when the run resumes.

PromotionCause.description:
Where a run's promotion leads: the node that exhausted its re-routes,
and the node it was routed to.

failure.description:
The failure that exhausted the node's re-routes, when a failure
asked for the promotion. Absent on a promotion the log wrote
without one.

PromotionSignaledPayload.description: A run asked to be run wider than the mode it started in.

cause.description:
What asked for the promotion. Absent from a log written before the
cause was recorded, which carries only the sentence `reason` holds.

evidence.description:
The record the promotion rests on, kept apart so a surface can show
it under its own heading.

suggested_mode.description:
The mode a successor would run in: the one `modes:` declares right
after the run's own, the only way a promotion moves.

ProposedCheck.description: A criterion a session proposed, and what running it found.

cmd.description: The command as the session wrote it.

precheck.description: What the engine's own run of the command found.

ProposedCriterion.description:
A command a session proposes with a scope request or a finding: one that
fails when proposed and passes once the work it asks for is done.

ProposedCriterionPrecheck.description: The code a proposed criterion exited with before the work.

Protection.description: Why a path is protected. The first reason that holds a path names it.

oneOf.description: The project's own `permissions.paths.deny`.
The configuration tree of the agent CLI a session runs under.
The instruction files an agent reads: the one reason a person may grant.
A test a person approved for a spec: no task writes it.
The run's own git register: `.git`, and what lies under it.

PublishedGate.description: Where the forge published the pull request a gate waits on.

PullRequestOpenedPayload.description:
A pull request a `pull_request` node opened — or found open, carrying
this run's marker, when it ran again — on the project's forge. Written
the moment the forge answers, before the node closes: the pull request
exists outside the run whatever the node does next.

head.description: The branch the run pushed, which the pull request carries.

number.description: The number the forge gave it.

QuestionFault.description:
What a rule of a questions document, or of the answers to one, found
wrong.

QuestionId.description: A question id: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

QuestionsAnsweredPayload.description:
The answers to a node's questions arrived, and how. The node is
`Running` again, owed the close its questions deferred.

answers_hash.description: The hash of the answers artifact.

responder.description: Who answered, when the channel says.

QuestionsAskedPayload.description:
A node handed its questions over and closed on them: what it asked
from, which ids await an answer, and what the session that asked
spent.

The pair of [`QuestionsAnsweredPayload`]. Between the two the node
waits, and the `node_finished` its close deferred lands after the
answer — so a node that asked is never mistaken for one that failed,
and a log that holds a questions document is never mistaken for a
node that is waiting on it.

questions.description:
The ids awaiting an answer. Never empty: a node with nothing to
ask finishes in the same close instead of waiting.

questions_hash.description:
The questions document the node handed over: what the answers
answer, and what the round re-reads before putting them to
anyone.

tokens_used.description:
What the session that asked spent. The attempt's accounting
closes here, so the `node_finished` after the answer carries
none and no surface counts the session twice while it waits.

RailEvent.description: When in a session a CLI asks.

oneOf.description: A file tool is about to write.
A file tool wrote.
The session is about to end its turn, and with it its work.

RailFailedPayload.description: A failure of the rail, with the moment it was for and its closed cause.

cause.description: The closed reason the rail failed.

event.description: The moment the failed call was for; absent when none could be read.

session_id.description: The session the failure belongs to; absent when no session does.

RailFailureCause.description:
The causes a failure reaches the log under: a closed set, so every
surface names a cause the same way.

oneOf.description: A call or an answer that does not read.
The engine refused the session's credential.
The engine did not answer within the window.
A formatter could not be started.
The listener that serves the session stopped.
A stop's judgement failed, and the stop went on.
The session asked with no fence to judge its writes by.

RailSummaryPayload.description: What a session's rail calls took, written once when the session closes.

model.description: The model the rail heard first, when a hook named one.

moments.description: One histogram per moment that was asked.

Reach.description: A path a request reaches, and the protection that holds it.

RedCheck.description:
Why a judging check came out red: a coverage figure under its
threshold or none at all, a command that exited non-zero, or a baseline
suite that passed when it was measured and fails in this check.

oneOf.description:
The coverage the run measured, when it measured one, and the
threshold it fell short of. `cmd` is the command that measured it.

The command that exited non-zero, with its exit code, the line it
concluded with and the run object holding everything it printed.

The baseline suite passed when the lineage measured it and fails in this check;
`tail` is what it printed last, which says why.

RefusalCause.description: Why a session refused the request.

oneOf.description: Unclassified: final for this attempt, never re-attempted on its own.
The credential the session used was refused.
The model the session asked for is not one the account can use.
Transport markers only; the one cause the engine re-attempts by itself.

The CLI could not keep the session's conversation within the model's
context window. This session cannot go on, though its work can: the
engine hands it to one fresh session, which carries none of that
conversation.

Remedy.description: One option a failure's menu offers, with the input it waits for.

precondition.description: The input a `retry` waits for; always set on one. Other options may leave it `None`.

Report.description:
Every problem one document has, reported together.

Collecting them is not a convenience: a reader who corrects one
problem per round pays a round per problem, and a writer who hears
one rule at a time rewrites the document once per rule.

RequestedScope.description:
What a node's session asked to be allowed to write, and why, in its
own words.

RerouteOrigin.description:
What caused a `node_rerouted`. The two mechanisms differ in kind: an
`on_failure` reroute is a bounded retry (it carries counters); a
gate's `on:` choice is a routing decision (it carries none).

ReservedIdentity.description:
A name under a node's artifact view that the engine writes itself,
so an opaque artifact may not claim it.

The run's view of a node holds one file per identity, and an
interpreted artifact is written from the document the engine
accepted. A declared name equal to one of those would put two
writers on one path, and the file a reader opened would say nothing
about which of them wrote it.

oneOf.description: The view of the document of this kind: `<kind>.yaml`.

Responder.description: A responder: not empty and without control characters

RuleCode.description:
The stable name of a rule that only holds across a whole
document.

Exhaustive, so a rule cannot be minted by typing a new string,
and countable, so a receipt reports what a run keeps getting
wrong without reading prose. A code says which rule broke and
nothing about which document it broke in: `DuplicateId` is one
rule asked of a workflow, a tasks document, findings and
questions alike, and what separates them is the
[`DocumentKind`](crate::diagnostic::DocumentKind) on the report carrying
it. Counting by code alone conflates them; counting by kind
and code does not.

Every variant belongs to some document's
[`RULES`](crate::shape::Document::RULES), so a rule the engine
enforces is a rule the writer was told about before writing.

oneOf.description: A second entry already carries this id.

Every criterion is a guard, so nothing in the task proves work
happened.
`depends_on` names a task nobody declared.
Two independent tasks reach for the same files.
A second shape already carries this name.
A second decision already carries this id.
A shape's `owner` names a task nobody declared.
A shape lives in a file its owner's scope does not cover.
A task `uses` a shape nobody declared.
A task uses a shape without waiting for the task that builds it.
A task says it changes a place its scope does not cover.
A second spec already names this task.
A spec lists no test.
A test does not say what passing it proves.
A test file's path leaves the repository, or reaches into `.git`.
A second file of the document already has this path.
A spec names a task the run's plan does not declare.
A spec's file names a path the run's tree already holds.

A spec written again for a departure changes the tests of a task
nobody departed from.

A spec written again for a departure gives the task departed from
the tests it had.

A criterion's command never answers where the engine runs
criteria: it is not found, not executable, or never returns.
A criterion that has to fail before the work already passes.
A guard that has to pass before the work already fails.

A finding's proposed criterion already passes on the run's tree,
so passing it later proves no fix.
A plan a person reviews says nothing of what it changes in one line.

A plan, or one of its tasks, that a person reviews does not say
what it does and why.
A criterion of a plan a person reviews does not say what it proves.

A task of a plan a person reviews does not say what a person sees
once it is done.

A task of a plan a person reviews does not say what it changes,
where.
A decision of a plan a person reviews does not say why.
A change of a plan a person reviews does not show its code.

A change of a plan a person reviews shows code that leaves out a
symbol its `at` names.

A change of a plan a person reviews shows a comment where its code
goes.

A criterion passes once a name is written in a file its task
changes, whatever the code does.
Two tasks are judged by the same command.

A criterion, or a spec's test, runs the project's tests without
extending the suite the run measures.
A task `uses` a shape it builds itself.

A task changes the test file its criterion runs, where the spec
writes the tests.
A task changes a file the run's spec wrote.
A decision answers a question no person answered in the run.
A file a spec writes is run by none of its tests.
A test of a spec runs none of the files the spec writes.
An update or a withdrawal names a finding this node never posted.

A withdrawn id is final — it is not posted, updated or withdrawn
again.
A withdrawal does not say why.
`answer_type` is `choice` and `values` is empty.

An optional question does not say what the work assumes when
nobody answers it.
A `required` question has no answer.
An answer's value is not what its question's `answer_type` allows.

A `mode` leaves out a node the workflow cannot run without, or a
node a node it includes reroutes to.

`invariant: true` on a child of a `parallel` group, where nothing
honors it: modes and re-verification read the top level.

`optional: true` where leaving the node out would leave the run
without something it cannot do without: on a child of a
`parallel` group, or on a node a required one re-routes to or
reads from.

RunCreatedPayload.description:
The run is born: the manifest it froze, by hash, and what it decided
once, at birth, so that no wake reads a config or a workflow again to
know what the run is. The first event of every run's log.

base_branch.description: The branch the run starts from, as the manifest froze it.

base_commit.description: The commit the run starts from, as the manifest froze it.

checkout.description:
The checkout of its own the run works in. Absent for a run working
in a person's checkout, and from a log written before it was
recorded, where the run's checkout is the one named after it under
the worktrees root its manifest froze.

environment.description:
What the run's commands ran with when it was born. Absent from a
log written before it was recorded. Boxed: every stored event is
as large as the largest payload, and this one is read once.

inputs.description:
Every declared input as the manifest froze it, given or defaulted,
already validated.

left_out.description:
The optional nodes this run leaves out because its config lacks
what they need, and the nodes only they lead to. Decided once,
here, so replay never re-reads a config to know its own graph.

manifest_hash.description:
The hash of the manifest the run froze: what the log's hash chain
is anchored on.

mode.description:
The mode the run was created in. A run never changes mode: a
promotion creates a successor run.

opens_on_base.description:
Whether the run's tree, when it was born in a checkout of its own,
held exactly the commit it opened on — what lets the suite be
measured in another checkout of that commit while the run goes
on. Absent — false — for a run working in a person's checkout, one
whose tree held more, and a log written before the field: those
measure in their own tree, before anything changes it.

promoted_from.description:
The run this one succeeds, when a promotion created it. The link
lives here, never in the run's id.

yunta_schema.description:
The workflow's `yunta_schema` range as declared, or the binary's own
schema when the workflow declares none.

RunFault.description:
What the run found when it ran a document's commands, or read a spec
against the plan and the tree the run holds.

oneOf.description:
A command that never answered: `said` is the line it concluded with,
and `environment` the shell and `PATH` it ran under.
A program a criterion starts that is on no directory of the run's `PATH`.
A criterion that passes before the work: `said` is the line it concluded with.
A guard that is red before the work: `said` is the line it concluded with.
A finding's proposed criterion that already passes on the run's tree.
`planned` is the plan's tasks; absent when the run holds no plan.
A test file a spec writes at a path the run's tree already holds.
A spec written again for a departure gives the departed task the tests it had.
A spec written again for a departure changes the tests of another task.
A spec written again for a departure leaves out a task's spec the run holds.

RunFinishedPayload.description:
A run closed: how, and the metrics it closed with. A closed run spends
what these record, with nothing left in flight.

closed_by.description:
The person who closed a run nobody was going to continue. Absent
for a run the engine closed by driving it to its end.

metrics.description:
The run's spend at the close, derived from the log and never
estimated: what settled and what was still in flight, together.

RunId.description: A run id: one path segment: printable ASCII without whitespace, `/` or `\`, and not `.` or `..`

RunMetrics.description:
A run's spend in tokens, the only unit the engine counts in: a price is a
surface's estimate beside it, never this.

cptv.description:
The cost per verified task: `tokens` over the tasks that reached
`done`. Absent when none did.

RunMovedPayload.description:
The run moved, between two of its steps, into another checkout of its
project's pool that already built the commit the run stands at — as a
rule, the one its last unit worked in — and works there from here on.

RunPausedPayload.description: Why the run is parked: the pause the engine recorded, as a fact.

RunResumedPayload.description:
A run woke, once it verified it still holds what its log says: the
policy each node the log left running resolved to, what its commands
run with from here, and — when they changed while it was parked — its
checkout and its tree.

checkout.description:
The checkout the run works in from this wake on, when it is not the
one it worked in before: the one it last held was given back while
it was parked.

environment.description:
What the run's commands run with from this wake on. Absent from a
log written before it was recorded.

policies.description:
Every node the log left running with no terminal event, and the
`on_interrupt` it resolved to: its own, or the config's default.

tree.description:
The run's tree as this wake found it, recorded when a node's failure
waited on a person: a change a person made to the tree while the run
was parked reaches the log here. Absent on every other wake.

RunToolFailedPayload.description:
One failed call to a tool this binary serves on `yunta-run`, as the CLI
reported rejecting it. Not a terminal: it does not say the node failed
because of the call, and it holds no argument, answer or error text.

session_id.description: The session that made the call.

RunToolFailureCause.description:
The closed reason a run tool call failed, without adapter error text:
`approval_blocked`, the call never reached the server because the CLI
held it back, or `call_failed`, the server received it and answered with
an error.

RunToolRefusal.description:
Why this binary refused a call to one of the tools it serves on
`yunta-run`: a closed set, so the log says it without the prose the
session was answered with.

oneOf.description:
A request of the same kind was already written and waits on a
decision.
The call's arguments do not say what the tool needs.
The tool is not one this session may call here.
The finding the call names cannot be answered the way it asks.
The document handed over was refused, or was already superseded.
The engine could not do what the call asked of it.

RunToolRefusedPayload.description:
A call to a tool this binary serves that it refused, and why, written by
the listener that refused it. A call a stop cut short — the run's, its
task's or its session's — was refused by nothing, and leaves none.

RunnerCandidate.description:
One candidate of a runner in `runners:`: the adapter, the model it asks
that adapter's CLI for, and optionally an agent and an effort.

Three words, three things. An adapter is the integration with one agent
CLI (`claude-code`, `codex`, `mock`); a runner is the binding a node asks
for by name — the role a workflow needs, `runner: planner`, which the
project's config fills with the CLIs it has; an agent is a set of
instructions the run owns, added to the CLI's own.

agent.description:
The agent this candidate's sessions work under; a node's own
`agent:` wins over it, so the candidates of one runner may each
pair their adapter with an agent of its own.

effort.description:
How long the model reasons, unless the node says otherwise; absent
leaves it to the CLI.

RunnerName.description: A runner name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

RunnerRefusal.description: Why a node's runner did not resolve to an adapter a run can use.

oneOf.description: No `runners:` entry defines the runner.
None of the runner's candidates is available; `tried` names the adapters it looked at.

RunnerRejection.description:
Why a runner candidate was not used. A log written before the typed
reason stored the sentence, which reads back as `Recorded { sentence }`.

oneOf.description: The run's `--adapter` flag pinned another adapter.
The candidate's adapter is not available here.

A sentence an older log stored, kept as written. The field is
named: a newtype variant of `String` does not serialize under an
internal tag.

RunnerResolvedPayload.description:
`runner` names the `runners:` entry the node resolved through. The
reader also accepts `role`, the field's former name, so a log written
under it still replays.

A node with a session resolves its runner before it assembles its
context, which names the run tools the way that runner's CLI names
them: a node's `runner_resolved` comes before its `context_assembled`.

chosen.description:
The candidate the node runs on, with the node's own `agent:` and
`effort:` over the candidate's.

discarded.description: Every candidate passed over before the chosen one, and why.

SchemaRange.description: a schema range: whitespace-separated comparators (`>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `=`) over whole schema majors, e.g. `>=1 <2`

ScopeAsker.description: Who asked for the scope a denial refused.

denied.description:
The paths of the diff no session of the run may write, whatever
the scope allows: what the project denies to every run, and the
tests a person approved. Absent when there are none, and in a log
written before anything could be denied.

violations.description:
The paths of the diff the work may not change: outside every glob of
its scope, or denied to every run. Empty when the work stayed inside.

ScopeDerivedPayload.description:
What a task may write beyond its declared scope because a shape it owns
is named there — derived by the engine from the workflow's tasks and the
run's tree, never asked for and never decided. Not a grant: it counts
toward no cap.

at.description: The commit the files were read at.

common.description:
The shapes the task owns that so many files name that following
them would reach half the tree: they reach nothing.

paths.description:
Each file, exactly, outside the task's declared scope that names a
shape it owns. Replaces whatever an earlier derivation stated.

ScopeExpansionDeniedPayload.description:
A request for scope refused, and why. Every refusal also posts a
finding that says so.

count_this_run.description: The engine's grants in this run when the request was refused.

mode.description:
The mode in force when a loop denied it. A node's own denial has
none, and reads back without one.

task_id.description: Absent when the denied request was the node's own.

why.description:
Why it was denied, when the decider said. A denial logged as text
before reasons were typed is read by `why()` instead.

ScopeExpansionGrantedPayload.description: A request for scope granted: who decided, and exactly what it allowed.

count_this_run.description:
The engine's grants in this run once this decision is made: what
`max_per_run` caps. A person's grant is not one of them.

mode.description:
The mode in force when a loop granted it. A node's own grant has
none, and reads back without one.

paths.description:
The exact paths this grant authorized — self-contained
audit, and what a later attempt's effective scope derives from
the log, instead of re-pairing the grant with the
`requested` event that preceded it. `default` for logs written
before the field existed (tolerant reader).

task_id.description:
The task the grant widens. Absent for a grant to a node's own
scope — the node the event is written under.

ScopeExpansionMode.description:
How a loop node treats an agent's request to widen its scope.
Default `Deny`: a node that omits `scope_expansion:` entirely gets
the same behavior as one that declares it with no `mode:` — no
expansions, every request becomes a finding without interrupting.

ScopeExpansionRequestedPayload.description:
What a session asked to write beyond its scope, as it asked it: never a
request the engine rewrote. Written when the request is decided — at
the call, for a refusal no work could change, and otherwise at the
close of the attempt or the node that received it.

paths.description: The globs it asked to be allowed.

proposed_criterion.description: A criterion it proposed with the request, when it proposed one.

proposed_criterion_precheck.description:
What the proposed criterion did when the decision ran it before any
work; absent when the decision did not run it.

reason.description: Its reason, in its own words.

task_id.description:
The task that asked. Absent when the session that asked works a
node of its own rather than a task: the request is then that
node's, the one the event is written under.

ScopeExpansionWithdrawnPayload.description:
A request its task closed with, unanswered. Nobody decided it, so
nothing was granted or denied: the request leaves with the task,
posting no finding and counting toward no cap. A task that does not
close keeps its request for a person.

ScopeGlob.description: a scope glob: a path pattern where `*` stays within one directory and `**` recurses

ScopeWait.description: What a loop waits on in one scope request.

because.description: Why the request is not decided without a person.

paths.description:
The paths the request asks to be allowed. Empty on an older log, whose
record named them.

proposed.description: The criterion the session proposed for the request, if it proposed one.

Seq.description: A position in a run's log: a positive number

ServiceReachablePayload.description: The service a session lost answers again, and the session goes on.

waited_ms.description: How long the session waited for it, in the host's awake time.

ServiceUnreachablePayload.description:
A session cut off from the service behind it: it waits for the service
to answer, and goes on as the same session. Past the wait's bound no
`service_reachable` follows, and the session fails as any other does.

message.description: What the session's CLI said when it lost the service.

session_id.description: The session that lost its service, the one that goes on.

SessionDeath.description:
A session that ended without ever reporting a terminal event: whose
it was, and how its process went, when it had one of its own.

SessionEnd.description:
How the process ended: the status it exited with, or the signal that
ended it.

A closed union rather than two optionals, so a process that says
neither is not representable. A stored `type` this build does not
know reads back as [`SessionEnd::Unknown`] — the tolerance everything
persisted here gives a reader older than its writer.

SessionExit.description:
What a process left behind: how it ended, and the last lines it wrote
to stderr, redacted of every declared secret and session token.

SessionId.description: A session id: not empty and without control characters

SessionRefusal.description: A refusal kept whole: the adapter's message and its cause.

Shown.description:
An artifact an escalation puts in front of the person deciding: the
version they saw, by its hash, so a decision on it is a decision on
exactly those bytes.

content_hash.description: The exact bytes the person was shown.

producer.description:
The node that produced it; absent for what no node produced, such as
the run's findings — a view the log derives, which the run's store
keeps under this hash.

SkillName.description: A skill name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

SpecFault.description: What a rule of a spec document found wrong with it.

StatedClaim.description: An engine claim as the log holds it, tagged by `claim`.

StopRefusal.description: One reason a session's work would not close.

oneOf.description: A criterion of its task is red, or a guard after one waits.
It changed a path outside its scope.
A document its node declares was never handed over.
A document was handed over, and the close would refuse it.

StopRefusedPayload.description:
A session that asked to stop with work its close would not take, told
why and sent back to it — at most once for one state of that work.

state.description:
What the work stood at: the tree the session left and, for a
node's own session, what the run holds of the documents it owes.

task_id.description: The task a loop's session works; absent for a node's own session.

why.description: What kept the work from closing, in the order the close judges it.

Stuck.description: Why a failure offers no remedy.

oneOf.description: The config the run froze at birth lacks what this needs; a new run under a config that declares it is the way out.

A file the run froze at birth no longer holds the bytes it froze: the
run reads its copy, so a new run is the way out.
The project's permissions deny the work.
The scope needs a grant this run will not give.
The same check on the same tree answers the same: the tree has to change first.
A person's decision is owed before the node can go on.
The refusal says the same to every attempt.
A declared criterion no work of the plan can pass: the plan has to change.

SubmissionOutcome.description:
Accepted, and the file the engine wrote from it; or refused, and
every problem the document has.

Surprise.description:
What a criterion's first run told the engine before any work began.
Each case says the criteria are wrong, not the task.

oneOf.description:
A non-guard criterion that already passes before any work: the
criteria need fixing, not the task.

A guard already red on the tree the task starts from: what broke it
came before the task. `proves` is what the guard is there to show,
when the task or the run says so.
A criterion that never answered; `Unanswered::of(exit_code)` says why.

TaskCause.description:
Why a task stopped short of done. A `blocked` status carries one, and
the words a person reads for it are written by the render crate.

oneOf.description:
The criteria were wrong before any work started: what the
pre-check found, one entry per criterion.

Every attempt ran and the criteria are still red, or the work left
the scope the task declared. `red` and `outside` are what the last
attempt left: the criteria still failing, and the paths it changed
outside the scope.

After an attempt, a criterion never answered: its command could not
be found or executed, or it was stopped before it answered. Another
attempt would change the tree, never that.

The session refused the request, with the adapter's message and the
cause it gave. The cycle ends here: no other session runs the task.
The account's limit ended the session; the node waits for its reset.

The session an attempt worked in ended without a terminal event, and
how its process went.

A person chose to continue from the work the task's last attempt
left, and that work no longer applies on the run's tree: these are
the paths it conflicts on.

A criterion's own command is one the run's permissions refuse, so
the task cannot be verified at all. `rule` is the command and the
list that refused it.

A scope-expansion request is owed a human decision, and no further
session spends budget while one is owed.

The session declared that its work departs from the plan, and a
person answers each departure before the task closes.

The session declared a criterion impossible on the plan's work. No
further session retries it, and the planner rewrites the tasks.

TaskCheckAnsweredPayload.description:
What that judgement answered the session, and how long it took.

Audit: a check judges work in progress, and only the attempt's close
moves the task. The question is written before the judgement runs, so
a `task_check_started` with no answer after it is a check whose
session ended first, or whose answer never reached it.

closes.description: Whether the task would have been done had the session ended then.

denied.description:
What it changed that no session of the run may write: what the
project denies to every run, or a test a person approved.

duration_ms.description:
How long the whole judgement took, answers taken from earlier runs
included.

outside_scope.description: What the work changed outside the task's scope.

results.description:
One result per criterion that ran or was answered by an earlier run
on the same tree, the guards the run holds every task to among them.

waiting.description:
The guards the check did not run, by command: a criterion that ran
before them — one of the task's own, or a guard — was red. Absent
when every guard ran.

TaskCheckStartedPayload.description:
A task session asked the engine to judge its work as it stands — the
judgement the attempt's close would make if the session ended now.

TaskFault.description: What a rule of a tasks document found wrong with it.

oneOf.description:
`cmd` is the criterion's command with its surrounding space trimmed,
as the clause names it.

`unreadable` is the report of a scope that does not compile, when that
is why the file cannot be shown to be covered.

`unreadable` is the report of a scope that does not compile, when that
is why the change cannot be judged against it.
`names` are the bare identifiers; the clause puts the backticks around them.

TaskId.description: A task id: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

TaskProbe.description:
How one task's criteria answered where a document's hand-over ran
them.

TaskRegisteredPayload.description:
A task of the run's tasks document, registered as the document states
it: what a status change, a check and a session read the task by.

criteria.description: Its criteria, a frozen copy of what the document declares.

depends_on.description: The tasks it waits on; empty, and absent, when it waits on none.

TaskStatus.description:
Where a task of the run stands: the token the log writes, and the word
every surface, document and agent reads. Not a node's word: a task is
`done` when its criteria pass and its work has landed, while a node
finishes when it ran, so a finished loop can leave tasks `blocked`.

TaskStatusChangedPayload.description:
A task moved, as the engine decided it, and the event that justifies
the move. Nothing else moves a task: no session has a tool that does.

caused_by.description: `seq` of the event that justifies this transition.

commit.description:
Where the task's work landed, on a `done` and nowhere else: the
commit the run's tree carried after integrating it. What makes a
`done` answerable by another run — a tree either descends from
this commit or does not have the work.

left_work.description:
The commit holding the work the task's last attempt left: on a
`blocked`, work a person can have the next cycle continue from;
on a `pending` a person reopened that way, the work it continues
from. Absent when the attempt left nothing, and on every other
transition.

resumes.description:
On a `pending` that reopens a task after the answer to a scope
request its session made: that session, which the next cycle
resumes on the same work. Absent on every other transition.

stop.description:
On a `blocked`: why the task stopped. Absent on every other
transition, and in a log written before the field.

TaskStop.description:
A task that stopped, and why: one entry of the list a loop's failure
carries for the tasks that kept it from closing.

TemplateVar.description:
Every variable a `{{…}}` may name.

What each one is worth is the renderer's to say — the engine fills a
node's, a mock fixture fills a scripted session's — but what they are
called is decided here and nowhere else.

TerminalState.description:
How a run closed: its work done, a failure that ended it, a person who
closed it, or a promotion. `cancelled` is a person closing a stopped run
nobody was going to continue (`yunta close`), and its `run_finished`
names who.

oneOf.description:
The run closed because its own gate accepted promotion
to a later-declared mode — never because the work itself failed
or was cancelled.

Timed.description: The wall-clock bound a run's work went past: a session's own, or an executor's.

oneOf.description: A session's wall-clock bound.
An executor's wall-clock bound.

TokenUsage.description:
Tokens a session reported, or a sum of such reports: what every budget
and every spend the engine derives is counted in.

cached.description:
The part of `input` the CLI read from its cache, when it says: a
part of the input, never added to it.

ToolNaming.description:
How a CLI names the tools of an MCP server it mounts, as its model
calls them: a rule over the server's name and the tool's, never a
table, so it names every tool — including one added after the
adapter was written.

oneOf.description: The tool's own name: `yunta_task`.
`mcp__<server>__<tool>`, the server's name as it was configured.

`mcp__<server>__<tool>`, with every `-` of the server's name
written `_`.

ToolTarget.description:
What a tool call acted on, as the log may carry it.

A tool's argument is the session's own text: a path, a shell command,
a URL. Some of it names the repository, which a reader needs; some of
it is whatever the session typed, which may be anything at all,
including a secret. So the log carries two things and they are not
the same thing: `display` is what a reader may be shown and is only
ever present for a value the engine itself can vouch for, and
`digest` is what identifies the target — the whole hash, so two
targets never share one. `abbreviated()` is how a hash is shown,
never how it is stored.

digest.description: What identifies the target, whether or not it can be shown.

display.description:
The target as a reader may see it. Absent whenever the value is
the session's own text.

TreeId.description: A tree id: 7 to 64 lowercase hex digits: a git object id, abbreviated or full

Unbuildable.description:
Why a session's confinement cannot be built as asked, or an adapter
cannot apply it.

oneOf.description: A session whose commands run unconfined has no sandbox to close its network with.
A writable root inside the checkout would admit writes the scope does not.

Unchanged.description:
The attempt that last actually ran on the tree a refused attempt
would have run on, and what it failed with.

UnknownVariable.description: A `{{…}}` naming something that is not a variable.

UnpassableTask.description:
A task whose declared criterion no work of the plan can pass: the
criterion's command, and the reason its session declared it with.

Waiting.description: Why a request waits for a person instead of being decided.

oneOf.description: `ask` mode: every request waits.
Another task of the batch may write one of the paths.
The request reaches an instruction file, which only a person grants.
A node's request that a person answers.

WhyWithheld.description:
Why an option is withheld: the flaws of the plan it would take the run
past, or the words an older log stored.

WithdrawalCause.description: Why a request left without an answer.

oneOf.description: The task closed while its request still waited for an answer.

Withheld.description: An option the gate withholds, and why.

WorkflowFault.description: What a rule of a workflow found wrong with it.

oneOf.description:
`nearest` is the id the typed one most likely misspells, among the
workflow's ids other than the node's own.

`node` and `other` are the two children whose scopes overlap; the
diagnostic's subject is their group.

Worktree.description: What the session's file tools may write under the checkout.

oneOf.description: Nothing under the checkout.
The files the node's scope names.
Every file under the checkout.

WriteFormattedPayload.description:
What the engine formatted the moment a session wrote it. The formatters
of one write share the rail's format window, and one still running when
it closes is cut: `-2` and `timed_out`.

changed.description: The ones whose content it changed.

duration_ms.description: How long the command took, which the session waited.

exit_code.description: How the command exited; `-2` when the window cut it.

output.description:
What the command printed, redacted and kept under its hash. Absent
when the store did not keep it, and in logs written before this field.

paths.description: Every file it was handed, relative to the worktree.

run.description: The project command that formatted them.

timed_out.description: Whether the bound stopped the command before it finished.

WriteRefusedPayload.description:
A write the fence refused before it happened. The engine writes it from
the session's rail, when the fence refuses a write the session's hook
asked about, before it answers the hook; no adapter reports one, so a
write a CLI's own sandbox denies is not here.

session_id.description: The session that was open when the fence refused the write.

target.description: What it was going to write, relative to the worktree when under it.
